									3746 text Refined the trace theorem Derived the workload tail bound Derived variance-sensitive bounds and selected one coordinate A stronger receiver result emerged during the comparison. The earlier bound required every logical phase to stay small. Error correction only needs a bound on the total weight of the phase expansion. Using that distinction, I can remove the register-size logarithm from the Gaussian storage guarantee, without reconstructing the noise rank. The conventional comparison also improved: with a physically implemented Pauli twirl, an outer code can certify a fixed memory operation from average local error data. I’m keeping both results—the coherent guarantee and the potentially cheaper randomized construction—with their different gate and randomness costs.
